title: Counter, Accumulator, and Sentinel
definition: Counters track occurrences, accumulators combine successive values, and sentinels signal a distinguished control condition.
purpose: Name common iteration-state roles so initialization, update, and exit are reviewable.
history: These patterns recur across imperative programming, input processing, statistics, and search.
mental_model: A counter answers how many, an accumulator answers what combined result, and a sentinel answers whether processing should stop or change mode.
analogy: Tally marks, a running cash total, and a stop sign model the roles; the analogy fails when one variable has multiple roles or sentinel values collide with valid data.
common_mistakes: Incrementing on every item instead of matches
Using a valid data value as sentinel
Dividing by zero after empty input
industry_notes: Separate state roles and document sentinel contracts, especially when external input is involved.
ai_notes: AI may initialize an accumulator incorrectly or choose a sentinel that is valid domain data.
interview_notes: Ask the learner to identify each variable role and empty-input behavior.
